messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testPValueNearZero` fails due to precision limitations when calculating very small p-values in the PearsonsCorrelation class. The test aims to verify that the p-value computed from a dataset with correlation coefficient r tending to 1 results in a p-value tending toward 0 but not exactly zero, specifically testing for a very small positive value around 1E-303.

The PearsonsCorrelation method `getCorrelationPValues()` calculates p-values using a T-distribution cumulative probability function. The p-value for the correlation coefficient r is calculated by transforming r into a t-statistic and then computing a two-tailed p-value from the T-distribution cumulative probability. The relevant code multiplies the complement of the cumulative probability of t by 2.

The T-distribution cumulative probability (`TDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability`) internally uses the regularized Beta function (`Beta.regularizedBeta`). This calculation involves floating-point arithmetic and is subject to limitations due to machine precision (machine epsilon). The current bug report highlights that the p-values cannot decrease smoothly past the precision limit (around 2.2e-16) and drop abruptly to zero beyond that.

The correlation coefficient is calculated using linear regression (`SimpleRegression.getR()`) which derives the correlation r, and this calculation itself seems correctly implemented.

The issue is a numerical precision problem in the calculation of extremely small p-values in the T-distribution's cumulative probability function used by the PearsonsCorrelation class. This limitation causes the very small expected p-values near zero not to be accurately represented, leading to results that vanish suddenly rather than diminish smoothly, causing the test failure.

No recent bug reports appear directly related. The problem is effectively the same kind of floating-point precision limitation pointed out in the referenced similar issue (MATH-201) for t-test p-values.

Hence, the root cause is the machine epsilon (precision limit) in the statistical distribution probability functions used for p-value calculation, especially the T-distribution implementation's cumulative probability method. This leads to the failure of the test designed to check very small p-values in PearsonsCorrelation.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
